speaker: Videographer
text: We are now on the record. This is the videotaped deposition of Witness B, taken in connection with the wrongful death action arising from the collision on U.S. Highway 27A at Northeast 140th Court on May 7, 2016. Today's date is the fourteenth. The time on the video monitor is 9:02 a.m. Will counsel please state their appearances for the record.

speaker: Attorney
text: Good morning. I represent the estate of the driver of Vehicle A, the plaintiff in this matter, and I'll be conducting the examination today.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Good morning. I appear on behalf of the defendant motor carrier and the driver of Vehicle T. We'll reserve all objections except as to form until the time of trial, and the witness will read and sign.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's agreed. Is there anyone else present in the room that should be noted?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: No one else on our side.

speaker: Attorney
text: Nor on ours. Would the court reporter please swear the witness.

speaker: Videographer
text: Let the record reflect the witness has been sworn by the court reporter. Counsel, you may proceed.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Good morning.

speaker: Witness B
text: Good morning.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you please state your name for the record. For purposes of this video we'll refer to you as Witness B, and that's how you'll be identified in the transcript.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay. I understand. I gave my full name to the reporter before we started.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. You understand that you've just taken an oath to tell the truth?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, I do.

speaker: Attorney
text: And that oath is the same oath you would take if you were testifying in a courtroom in front of a judge and a jury?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, I understand that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you ever had your deposition taken before?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. This is my first time. I've never been in anything like this.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you ever testified in court, in any kind of case?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I got called for jury duty one time, years ago, but they sent me home the first day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you ever been a party to a lawsuit? Meaning you sued someone or someone sued you?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, never.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Since this is your first deposition, let me go through a few ground rules. They help keep the record clean, and frankly they make the day go faster. Is that okay?

speaker: Witness B
text: Sure.

speaker: Attorney
text: The court reporter is taking down everything that's said in this room, and the camera is recording you. So it's important that you answer out loud. A nod of the head or a shrug doesn't show up in the transcript. Do you understand?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Along the same lines, try to avoid answers like uh-huh or huh-uh. They look nearly the same on paper. Yes or no is better when it fits.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay. I'll try. I'm a talker, so you might have to remind me.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's perfectly fine. Second, please let me finish my question before you start your answer, even if you think you know where I'm going. And I'll do my best to let you finish your answer before I ask the next one. If we talk over each other, the reporter can't take us both down. Fair?

speaker: Witness B
text: That's fair.

speaker: Attorney
text: Third, if you don't understand a question, please tell me, and I'll rephrase it. If you go ahead and answer, I'm going to assume you understood the question. Is that reasonable?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fourth, I don't want you to guess. If you know something, tell me. If you don't know, it's perfectly fine to say I don't know or I don't remember. Do you understand the difference between a guess and an estimate?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think so. Can you explain what you mean?

speaker: Attorney
text: Sure. If I asked you how long this table is, you probably couldn't tell me exactly, but you could look at it and give me a reasonable estimate. That's fine. What I don't want is for you to make something up about something you never saw or heard.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay. That makes sense. So if I don't know, I just say so.

speaker: Attorney
text: Exactly. And if you're giving me an estimate, it helps if you tell me that it's an estimate.

speaker: Witness B
text: All right.

speaker: Attorney
text: From time to time the other attorney may object to one of my questions. Unless you're instructed not to answer, you should go ahead and answer the question after the objection. The objection is just for the record. Understood?

speaker: Witness B
text: So I still answer even when he objects.

speaker: Attorney
text: Correct, unless you're told otherwise.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: If you need a break at any time, just let me know. The only thing I'd ask is that you not take a break while a question is pending. Answer the question, and then we can take a break. All right?

speaker: Witness B
text: That's fine. I'm okay for now.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are you taking any medication today, or is there anything else that would affect your ability to understand my questions or give truthful and complete answers?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's understandable. Is there any reason at all you can't give your best testimony today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I can do it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Good. Let's start with a little background. Where do you currently live? I don't need a street address, just generally.

speaker: Witness B
text: I live here in the county. Out on the west side, kind of in between towns.

speaker: Attorney
text: How long have you lived in the county?

speaker: Witness B
text: About fourteen years now. Going on fifteen.

speaker: Attorney
text: And before that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Before that I lived a couple of counties north. I moved down here when my sister did. We're close, so we wanted to be near each other.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you live with anyone?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just me now. My son lived with me until a few years ago, but he's grown and moved out.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where did you go to school?

speaker: Witness B
text: I went to high school up north, where I grew up. I graduated. And then later I took classes at the community college for my certificate.

speaker: Attorney
text: What certificate is that?

speaker: Witness B
text: For home health. I'm a certified home health aide.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is that what you do for work?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I've done it for about eleven years.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you describe for the jury what a home health aide does?

speaker: Witness B
text: I go to people's houses, mostly older folks, and help them with daily things. Getting around the house, meals, light housekeeping, making sure they take their medicine on time. Some days it's just keeping somebody company.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you work for an agency or for yourself?

speaker: Witness B
text: For an agency. They give me my clients and my schedule.

speaker: Attorney
text: How many clients do you typically see in a week?

speaker: Witness B
text: It changes. Usually three or four regular clients. Sometimes more if someone's out and they need me to fill in.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are your clients spread out around the county?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, all over. That's a big part of the job, really. I'm in the car a lot, going from one house to the next.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how many miles would you say you drive in a typical week for work?

speaker: Witness B
text: Oh, a lot. I'd guess a few hundred. I don't keep exact track. The agency reimburses some of it.

speaker: Attorney
text: So that's an estimate.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, that's an estimate. A few hundred.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you working as a home health aide in May of 2016?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Same agency.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you working on Saturday, May 7, 2016?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. That was my day off. I usually have Saturdays.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll come back to that day in a little while. I want to finish up some background first. Do you have a driver's license?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: How long have you been driving?

speaker: Witness B
text: Since I was sixteen. So a long time.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you need glasses or contact lenses to drive?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I have reading glasses, for close-up things. Paperwork, my phone, that kind of thing. But I don't need anything for driving or for seeing far away.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a restriction on your license for corrective lenses?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, there's no restriction.

speaker: Attorney
text: When was the last time you had your eyes checked?

speaker: Witness B
text: Before this happened, it would have been maybe a year or so before. They told me my distance vision was fine. That's when they said I could use the readers for close up.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer. Let me ask it more simply. As of May 2016, did you wear any glasses for seeing at a distance?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Only the reading glasses, and only for reading.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you have them with you today?

speaker: Witness B
text: They're in my purse. I might need them if you show me papers.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Feel free to use them whenever you need to. Do you have any problems with your hearing?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. My hearing is good.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now, before today, did you do anything to prepare for this deposition?

speaker: Witness B
text: I looked over my statement. The one I wrote for the deputy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's talk about that. You said a statement you wrote for the deputy. What is that?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few days after the accident, a deputy from the sheriff's office called me and asked if I would come in and write down what I saw. So I did. It's about a page, handwritten.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember about how many days after the crash that was?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think it was three or four days after. It was the next week, during the week. I remember I had to move a client's visit around to go in.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you wrote that statement yourself, in your own handwriting?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The deputy gave me a form and I wrote it out. He asked me a couple of questions, but I wrote it myself.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone tell you what to write?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. He just said write down what you saw, in your own words.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you sign it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, I signed it at the bottom and dated it.

speaker: Attorney
text: When did you review it in preparation for today?

speaker: Witness B
text: I read it again last night, and once a couple of weeks ago when I got the paper saying I had to come in.

speaker: Attorney
text: The paper you're referring to, is that the subpoena?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The subpoena.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where did you get the copy of the statement that you reviewed?

speaker: Witness B
text: I kept a copy. The deputy made me a copy that day, and I put it in a folder at home with the other papers.

speaker: Attorney
text: Other than your written statement, did you review any other documents to prepare for today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you look at any photographs of the scene?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any maps or diagrams?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any news articles, videos, anything on the internet about the crash?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I've stayed away from all that on purpose.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why is that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because I was there. I don't need to watch it on the news. It was hard enough the first time.

speaker: Attorney
text: I understand. Did you meet with any attorney before today to prepare for this deposition?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I talked to somebody from your office on the phone once to set up the date, but that was about scheduling.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you discuss the substance of what you saw during that call?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just the date and the time and where to come.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you spoken with anyone from the motor carrier, or any attorney representing them?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Has anyone ever asked you to change anything in your statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody.

speaker: Attorney
text: Having reread your statement last night, is there anything in it that you believe is wrong or that you'd like to change today?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I wrote what I remembered, and I still remember it the same way.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you talked to anyone else about today's deposition? Family, friends, coworkers?

speaker: Witness B
text: My sister knows I'm here. She drove me, actually. And I told my supervisor I needed the morning off. That's about it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you discuss the details of what you saw with your sister in preparing for today?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not to prepare, no. We talked about it right after it happened, of course. But not about today.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll get into those conversations later. I'd like to turn now to the location. Are you familiar with U.S. Highway 27A in this county?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, very.

speaker: Attorney
text: How are you familiar with it?

speaker: Witness B
text: I drive it all the time. It's the main road out my way. Several of my clients are off of it, and it's the way to get into town for groceries and the pharmacy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Specifically, are you familiar with the stretch of 27A near the intersection with Northeast 140th Court?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I go right through there.

speaker: Attorney
text: How often, back in 2016, would you say you drove through that particular stretch?

speaker: Witness B
text: At least once a week. Usually more. I had a client back then who lived a few miles past there, and I went out to her every Tuesday and Thursday.

speaker: Attorney
text: So at least weekly, and often twice a week?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. At least weekly. Sometimes more if I was running errands.

speaker: Attorney
text: And today, do you still drive through there?

speaker: Witness B
text: I do. Not as much as I used to. I'll be honest, I go another way sometimes now if I can.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you drove that stretch, which direction were you usually going?

speaker: Witness B
text: Both. Going out to my client I'd go one way, and coming back the other. So both directions.

speaker: Attorney
text: How long have you been driving that stretch of road?

speaker: Witness B
text: Since I moved down here. So about fourteen years.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, plenty of times. It's a little country store. I'd stop for a drink or gas or a snack between clients.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before May 7, 2016, had you ever seen an accident at that intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I'd never seen one there myself.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you ever been in an accident anywhere on 27A?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you ever been in any car accident, as a driver or a passenger?

speaker: Witness B
text: One time, a long time ago, somebody backed into me in a parking lot. Nobody was hurt. That's it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Other than that parking lot incident, have you ever witnessed a serious crash before May 7, 2016?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Never like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now, I'm going to ask you some general questions about the road itself. I'm not asking about that day yet, just about the road as you know it from driving it. All right?

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is 27A in that area a divided highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It's two lanes going each way with grass in the middle.

speaker: Attorney
text: And what's the speed limit in that area, if you know?

speaker: Witness B
text: I believe it's sixty-five. That's what I've always gone by. I think there's a sign for it, but I couldn't swear to exactly where it is.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer, though I think you have. You said you believe it's sixty-five?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, I believe so. That's my understanding from driving it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is that stretch generally straight or curvy?

speaker: Witness B
text: Pretty straight through there. There's a hill to the west, coming toward the store from the west side. Not a big hill, but it rises up and then you come down toward the intersection.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll talk about the layout in more detail a little later. For now, generally, would you describe traffic on that stretch as heavy or light?

speaker: Witness B
text: It depends on the time of day. During the week, mornings and afternoons it can be busy. Weekends it's usually lighter. There are a lot of trucks, too.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Let me ask you about yourself for a moment. How tall are you?

speaker: Witness B
text: About five foot six.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was that the same in May of 2016?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I haven't grown any.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Do you have any medical condition that affects your balance or your ability to stand for long periods?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I'm on my feet all day at work. Standing is no problem.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask you about one more document before we move on. You mentioned the folder at home where you kept a copy of your statement. Is there anything else in that folder relating to this crash?

speaker: Witness B
text: The subpoena. And a card the deputy gave me with his name and number. That's all.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you ever write down any notes of your own, apart from the statement for the deputy?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't write anything else.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you ever take any photographs that day, with a phone or a camera?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't take any pictures.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you received any payment or anything of value for your testimony today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody's paid me anything. I lost a morning of work, if anything.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you have any relationship with the family of the driver of Vehicle A?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't know anybody involved.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any relationship with the motor carrier, or anyone who works for it?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you have any interest in the outcome of this case?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I just came because I was asked to say what I saw. I don't have anything riding on it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before I move on to the afternoon itself, I want to make sure we're on the same page about one thing. When I use the term Vehicle A, I'm referring to the dark four-door sedan that was involved in the collision. When I use the term Vehicle T, I'm referring to the tractor with the white trailer. Will you understand those terms if I use them?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The car and the truck.

speaker: Attorney
text: Exactly. And if at any point you're not sure which vehicle I mean, ask me.

speaker: Witness B
text: I will.

speaker: Attorney
text: And when I refer to the intersection, I mean where 27A meets Northeast 140th Court, by the store. Is that clear?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, that's clear.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. One last question on background. Is there anything about that day, May 7, 2016, that makes it stand out in your mind, apart from the crash itself?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a normal Saturday. I was off, I went shopping, I was waiting on my sister. If it hadn't been for what happened, I wouldn't remember anything about that day.

speaker: Attorney
text: But you do remember it.

speaker: Witness B
text: I remember it very well. I don't think I'll ever forget it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. I want to turn now to that afternoon in more detail.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'd like to turn now to the afternoon of Saturday, May 7, 2016. Do you remember that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I remember it very well. I don't think I'll forget it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why were you in the area of US-27A and Northeast 140th Court that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: I was waiting for my sister. She was supposed to pick me up at the store there after I finished my shopping.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which store are we talking about?

speaker: Witness B
text: The little store on the corner there, on the south side of the highway. They sell a bit of everything. Feed, drinks, snacks, some hardware.

speaker: Attorney
text: And how did you get to the store that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: A neighbor dropped me off. My car was in the shop that week, so I was getting rides from people.

speaker: Attorney
text: About what time did your neighbor drop you off?

speaker: Witness B
text: Around ten after four. Maybe a minute or two either way.

speaker: Attorney
text: How do you know it was around ten after four?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because my sister texted me she'd be there around five, and I remember thinking I had close to an hour to kill.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did your sister in fact arrive around five?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Right about five. A little after, maybe, because of everything that was going on by then.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll get to that later. When you were dropped off, what did you do first?

speaker: Witness B
text: I went inside and did my shopping. I picked up a few things. Some bread, a jug of tea, some batteries, and a bag of birdseed for my mother.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long were you inside the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Fifteen minutes, maybe. Not long. It's not a big store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you pay for your items?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. At the counter.

speaker: Attorney
text: And after you paid, where did you go?

speaker: Witness B
text: I went back outside. Out front of the store, to wait for my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why did you wait outside rather than inside?

speaker: Witness B
text: It was a nice day. And it's a little stuffy in there. I'd rather be outside than stand around in the aisles.

speaker: Attorney
text: So from the time you finished shopping until the collision, you were outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Outside, out front of the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you go back inside the store at any point before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed outside.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you sit down at any point while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: Off and on. I can't tell you exactly when. I was mostly standing.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask it differently. At the time of the collision, do you recall whether you were standing or sitting?

speaker: Witness B
text: I was standing.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's talk about the conditions that afternoon. What was the weather like?

speaker: Witness B
text: Clear. Sunny. No rain at all. It was warm but not hot like summer gets.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any clouds that you recall?

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe a few way off. Nothing over us. It was a bright, clear afternoon.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had it rained earlier that day, to your knowledge?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I know of. The road was dry. Everything was dry.

speaker: Attorney
text: How do you know the road was dry?

speaker: Witness B
text: I could see it. There weren't any puddles, nothing shiny. It looked like a dry road on a sunny day.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about the light? Was it full daylight?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Full daylight. The sun was still pretty high.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you recall where the sun was in the sky, generally?

speaker: Witness B
text: Up and kind of over to the west. Behind the traffic coming from the west, I'd say. It wasn't down low yet.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there any haze, smoke, or fog in the area?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. None of that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any wind that you noticed?

speaker: Witness B
text: A little breeze. Nothing to speak of.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now, how would you describe the traffic on the highway while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: Light. It's a Saturday afternoon out there. You'd get a few cars, then nothing for a while, then a few more.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there trucks as well as cars?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some. Mostly cars and pickups. Every so often a bigger truck.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you estimate how many vehicles passed in, say, a minute?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Calls for speculation.

speaker: Attorney
text: If you can.

speaker: Witness B
text: I really can't give you a number. It wasn't busy. Sometimes a minute would go by and nothing passed at all.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about noise? What could you hear while you were standing outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: The cars going by, mainly. They make that whoosh at highway speed. Some birds. A radio from inside the store when the door opened.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there any construction or machinery running nearby?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not that I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was it loud enough that you'd have had trouble hearing someone talk to you?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Only when a truck went by. Otherwise it was pretty quiet out there.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'd like you to describe the road for us in words. We'll look at a map later in the day, but for now, just in your own words. Can you do that?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'll try.

speaker: Attorney
text: Start with the highway itself. How many lanes are there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Four. Two going east and two going west.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything separating the eastbound lanes from the westbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. A big grassy median in between. It's wide. Wider than a lot of roads around here.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you estimate how wide the median is?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'm not good with feet. Wide enough you could park a couple of trucks end to end across it, maybe. Sixty feet? I don't know.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Which side of the highway is the store on?

speaker: Witness B
text: The south side. The eastbound side.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the lanes nearest the store are the eastbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The eastbound lanes are closest. Then the median, then the westbound lanes on the far side.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a place where you can cross the median at that intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. There's a crossover. A cut in the median where you can go across from one side to the other.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a traffic light at that crossover?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. No light. No stop light, no blinking light. Just the cut through the median.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are there stop signs?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think there's a stop sign on the side road coming up to the highway. Not on the highway itself.

speaker: Attorney
text: On the highway, are there turn lanes near the crossover?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. There's a left-turn lane on each side, I believe. It's kind of cut into the median before the crossover so people can get out of the fast lane to turn.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's focus on the westbound side. Is there a left-turn lane for westbound traffic?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. If you're heading west and want to turn left onto 140th, you pull into that turn lane in the median and wait there.

speaker: Attorney
text: And from that westbound turn lane, a vehicle turning left would cross what?

speaker: Witness B
text: It'd go through the crossover and across both of the eastbound lanes, and then onto 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: Tell me about 140th Court. Which direction does it run from the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: South. It goes south off the highway, right there by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Does 140th Court continue north of the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I've ever seen. I've only ever known it to go south.

speaker: Attorney
text: What's 140th Court like? Is it paved?

speaker: Witness B
text: It's paved. It's a smaller road. Two lanes, one each way, no median. Some houses and fields down it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where is the store in relation to 140th Court?

speaker: Witness B
text: It's right on the corner. On the east side of 140th, where it meets the highway.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the store sits at the southeast corner of the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's right.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now I'd like to ask about the area to the west of the intersection. What's the land like in that direction?

speaker: Witness B
text: There's a hill. The highway comes over a rise to the west and then comes down toward the intersection.

speaker: Attorney
text: How far west is the top of that hill, roughly?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just your best sense, if you have one.

speaker: Witness B
text: A good ways. A quarter mile maybe. I've never measured it. When you drive it, you come over the top and then you can see the store down the hill in front of you.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is it a steep hill?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Gentle. It's not a big hill. It's just enough that you can't see what's past the top.

speaker: Attorney
text: And when you drive east on that stretch yourself, as you said you do weekly, what do you see when you come over that rise?

speaker: Witness B
text: You see the road go down and the intersection ahead, and the store on the right. It's pretty open from the top on down.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about east of the intersection? What is it like in that direction?

speaker: Witness B
text: Flatter. The highway runs on straight. There are fences, some yards and houses back off the road, some power poles along the side.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are there trees along the highway near the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some, back from the road. Not right on the shoulder. It's mostly grass along the edges.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are there any buildings at the intersection besides the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not right there, no. The store is the main thing. There are houses further off.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a parking area at the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. A gravel and dirt lot in front and along the side. People pull in off the highway or off 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: How many cars were parked there while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: A couple. One or two. It wasn't busy. People would pull in, run in, and leave.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any vehicles parked between the store and the highway while you were outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember. Not big ones. Maybe a car came and went.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll move on. Is the shoulder of the eastbound lanes paved?

speaker: Witness B
text: There's a paved strip along the edge and then grass. Then the store lot.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there a speed limit sign anywhere near there that you know of?

speaker: Witness B
text: There's one somewhere back up the road. I believe it's sixty-five out there, but don't hold me to it.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: You're not certain of the posted limit?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, I'm not certain. That's just what I think it is from driving it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me go back to what you had with you that afternoon. When you went outside after shopping, what were you carrying?

speaker: Witness B
text: My purse, and a shopping bag. One of those plastic bags from the store with my things in it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just one bag?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just the one. The birdseed was the heaviest thing. I had it all in one bag.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which hand were you holding it in?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'd switch. It was heavy. I think I had it in my left hand most of the time, with my purse on my right shoulder.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you set the bag down at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: I might have, on and off. I don't remember exactly. When everything happened, I know I still had it, because I remember it banging against my leg when I jumped.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say you jumped, what do you mean?

speaker: Witness B
text: From the noise. The crash. It made me jump. That's all.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll come to the crash in detail later. Did you have a cell phone with you that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. In my purse.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you using your phone while you were waiting outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not right then. Earlier I'd read my sister's text, when I first got there. After that it was in my purse.

speaker: Attorney
text: So in the minutes before the collision, were you looking at your phone?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was in my purse. I wasn't on it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you talking to anyone on the phone in the minutes before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I called my sister after. Not before.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you texting, reading, or doing anything with the phone?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I know people will say I was on my phone, but I wasn't. I was just standing there watching the road.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Move to strike the last part as nonresponsive.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you listening to anything? Earbuds, headphones, music?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing in my ears.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing glasses that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I only wear reading glasses, and those were in my purse.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you need glasses to see things at a distance?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. My distance vision is fine. I just need the readers for small print.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing sunglasses?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't have sunglasses with me that day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the sun bother you at all while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It wasn't in my face. I could see fine.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing a hat or anything with a brim?

speaker: Witness B
text: No hat. Just my hair pulled back.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was anyone with you while you were outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I was by myself.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you talking with anyone in person while you waited?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not really. A man said hello going into the store. That's about it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know who that man was?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Never seen him before. Just somebody stopping in.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see where he went after that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Inside. I don't know after that. I wasn't paying him any attention.

speaker: Attorney
text: While you were waiting, what were you doing, generally?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just waiting. Watching the road, watching for my sister's car. She'd be coming from the west, so I kept looking that way.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why would your sister be coming from the west?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because she lives west of there. She'd come down the highway over that hill, same as anybody coming from that direction.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you were watching westbound or eastbound traffic for her?

speaker: Witness B
text: Eastbound. She'd be heading east toward me, coming down the hill.

speaker: Attorney
text: What kind of car does your sister drive?

speaker: Witness B
text: A little silver hatchback. I was looking for that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you watch the cars that came over the hill while you waited?

speaker: Witness B
text: Every one of them. Every time something came over I'd look to see if it was her.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there anything that afternoon, before the collision, that seemed unusual to you about the traffic?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a normal afternoon. Cars going by. Nothing unusual until it happened.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice any vehicles pulling into or out of the store lot in the few minutes before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't remember any right then. It was quiet.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice anyone walking along the highway, or crossing it?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody walking.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any bicycles or motorcycles?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any emergency vehicles, police cars, anything with lights, before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not before. Afterward, yes, a lot of them.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask one more general question about where you were. Throughout the time you were waiting, where were you?

speaker: Witness B
text: Outside. Out front of the store. I've said that.

speaker: Attorney
text: You have. I'm just making sure the record is clear. Did you go around to the side or back of the store at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed out front.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you walk out toward the highway at any point before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you cross 140th Court at any point before the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you ever waited outside that store before, on another day?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few times. When I've gotten rides. It's an easy place for people to pick me up.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you were familiar with what the intersection looks like from the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I know what it looks like from there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before May 7, had you ever seen a collision at that intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Never. I'd heard people say it's a bad crossing, but I'd never seen anything.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Move to strike as hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll ask you just about what you saw yourself. Before that day, had you yourself seen any near misses there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I can remember. Nothing that stuck with me.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. In the minutes leading up to the collision, about how long had you been standing outside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Ten minutes. Maybe a little more. I'd finished shopping at around twenty-five after, so ten or twelve minutes.

speaker: Attorney
text: And how are you estimating that?

speaker: Witness B
text: From when I got there and how long I was inside. I didn't look at a clock. It's my best guess.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. Did anything distract you in those minutes before? Any noise, anything that pulled your attention away from the road?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that. I was just looking at the road for my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you hungry, tired, not feeling well, anything of that sort that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I felt fine. I'd had lunch. I was a little tired from the week, but nothing out of the ordinary.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you had anything to drink that day other than water or tea?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Tea and water. That's all.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you taking any medication that affects your vision or your memory?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. I think that covers the background of the afternoon. Next I want to move to the traffic you saw coming from the west, beginning with the first time you noticed the car. Before I do, is there anything about the conditions or the road we've discussed that you want to add or correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I think I've said it. It was clear, it was quiet, and I was out front waiting.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's turn now to the car itself. You told me a few minutes ago that you were outside, out front of the store, when it happened. I want to take this slowly. When did you first notice the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: When it came over the hill. Off to the west, to my left if I'm facing the road. That's where I first saw it.

speaker: Attorney
text: The hill crest you described earlier, the one about a quarter mile or so to the west?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It comes over that rise and then it's sort of downhill toward the intersection.

speaker: Attorney
text: What was it about the car that made you notice it?

speaker: Witness B
text: It was dark, and it was by itself. There wasn't anybody right behind it or right in front of it. It just kind of stood out coming down the hill.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you describe the car for me?

speaker: Witness B
text: A dark car. A sedan, four doors I think. Low to the ground. Black or a real dark color, I couldn't tell you exactly which.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which direction was it traveling?

speaker: Witness B
text: East. Coming toward the intersection from the west, heading east.

speaker: Attorney
text: How well could you see the car as it came toward the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: I had a clear view of the car the whole way in. I watched it right up until the moment it hit. Nothing was in the way.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can go ahead. Is there anything you want to add to that answer?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. That's what happened. I saw it.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Let me break that down a little. When you first saw it at the top of the hill, about how far away would you say it was from the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Far. I don't know in feet. It was up at the top of the hill. However far that is.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. I don't want you to guess. Would it be fair to say it was some distance away?

speaker: Witness B
text: It was a good ways off, yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: And once you noticed it, did you keep looking at it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I kept looking at it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why did you keep looking at it?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't really know. I was waiting on my sister, so I was looking up the road anyway for her car. She'd be coming from that direction, from the west. So I was watching the cars come over the hill.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you were looking for your sister's car coming from the west?

speaker: Witness B
text: Right. She drives a light-colored car, so when I saw a dark one I knew it wasn't her, but I just kept watching it.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long did you watch that dark car before it reached the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not long. A few seconds. It was going pretty good.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say a few seconds, can you give me any better estimate than that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I wasn't counting. It wasn't a long time. It came down the hill and then it was there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's talk about speed. Do you have an estimate of how fast the car was traveling as it came down the hill?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Objection. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer if you have an estimate.

speaker: Witness B
text: It was fast. Highway speed. It wasn't slowing down that I could tell.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say highway speed, what do you mean by that?

speaker: Witness B
text: I mean like the other cars that go through there. People go fast on that road. It's a highway. It was going like a car on the highway goes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you put a number on it?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Same objection. Foundation.

speaker: Witness B
text: No, I can't put a number on it. I'm not going to make up a number. It was fast.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fair, and I don't want you to make up a number. Have you ever been trained in estimating vehicle speeds?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Ever worked in law enforcement, or as a crossing guard, anything like that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that. I take care of people in their homes. That's my job.

speaker: Attorney
text: Compared to the other eastbound traffic you had seen that afternoon while you were waiting, was the car going faster, slower, or about the same?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Witness B
text: I'd say about the same or maybe a little faster. I really couldn't tell you more than that. Everybody goes fast through there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the car change speed at any point as it came toward the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I saw. It looked like it was just going steady.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see any brake lights on the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: The car was coming toward me, sort of, so I wouldn't have seen brake lights on the back. I didn't see it slow down, is what I can tell you.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear any sound from the car as it approached, tires, anything like that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not really. There's wind out there and the road noise. I didn't hear any squealing or anything like that, if that's what you mean.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear any horn?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I don't remember any horn.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now, the eastbound side of the highway has two lanes, correct? You described that earlier.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, two lanes going east.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know which of the two eastbound lanes the car was in as it came down the hill?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think it was in the right one, the outside one, closer to my side. But I'm not a hundred percent on that.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say you think, how sure are you?

speaker: Witness B
text: Pretty sure. But I'm not going to swear on the lane. I'm sure it was going east and I'm sure I watched it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the car change lanes at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It stayed where it was, as far as I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the car move toward the shoulder or toward the median at any point before it reached the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It just came straight. Straight down the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any other vehicles in the eastbound lanes near that car at that time?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not near it. There might have been cars way back up the hill, I don't remember. Nothing right around it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any vehicles in the westbound lanes that you remember, other than the truck we'll talk about later?

speaker: Witness B
text: There might have been one or two going the other way. I don't remember anything specific about them.

speaker: Attorney
text: I want to go back to the hill for a moment. When the car first came over the crest, could you see the whole car, or just part of it?

speaker: Witness B
text: At first just the top of it, kind of, as it came over. Then the whole thing as it came down.

speaker: Attorney
text: And from that point on, could you see the whole car?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the sun a factor at all in how you were seeing the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. The sun was up high. It wasn't in my eyes. It was a bright afternoon, a nice day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing any glasses at that time?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I only wear my reading glasses, and those were in my purse. I don't need them for far away.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you doing anything else while you watched the car? Talking to anybody, looking at anything in your hands?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I had my bag, my shopping bag, but I wasn't doing anything with it. I was just standing there watching the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was anyone standing with you?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I was by myself out there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anybody walk in front of you or by you while you were watching the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody was out there. It was a slow afternoon.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear anything from inside the store at that time, music, anything that drew your attention?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. The door was shut. I was outside.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask it this way. Between the time you first saw the car at the top of the hill and the time it reached the intersection, did you look away at all?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Asked and answered.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't look away.

speaker: Attorney
text: Not even for a second, to look for your sister or anything else?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Once I saw that car I watched that car.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you looking at the car the entire time, or were you looking generally at the road?

speaker: Witness B
text: At the car. I was looking at the car.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why do you think you were so focused on that particular car?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Calls for speculation.

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't know why. It was coming fast and it was the only one. Sometimes you just watch something. I couldn't tell you why.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. As the car got closer to the intersection, did your view of it change in any way?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I could see it. It was closer, so I could see it better if anything.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you see the side of the car, the front of the car, which part?

speaker: Witness B
text: Mostly the side and a little of the front. It was going across in front of me, more or less, going from left to right.

speaker: Attorney
text: Going from your left to your right?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. West to east. Left to right the way I was facing.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you were facing the highway at that time?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I was facing the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you see whether there was anyone inside the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I couldn't see inside. The windows were dark and it was going too fast for that. I just saw the car.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not going to ask you anything about who was in the car or what anyone in the car was doing. I just want to be clear about what you could see. You saw the car itself, its body, its movement?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The car itself. Where it was and where it was going.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Now, as best you can, I want you to describe the last part of the car's approach, the last few seconds before it reached the intersection.

speaker: Witness B
text: It came down the bottom of the hill, it was coming straight, it didn't slow down, and then it went into the intersection, and that's when it hit.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say it hit, what did it hit?

speaker: Witness B
text: The truck. The trailer part of the truck. The big white trailer.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll talk about the truck in detail in a bit, so I don't want to get too far ahead. For now, I just want to stay with the car. Did you see the moment of contact?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you were looking at the car at the moment of contact?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Leading.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me rephrase. Where were you looking at the moment the car made contact with the trailer?

speaker: Witness B
text: At the car. I never lost sight of it. I watched it the whole way, right up until it hit.

speaker: Attorney
text: How confident are you in that?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'm confident. I know what I saw. People have asked me that and I tell them the same thing every time.

speaker: Attorney
text: Who has asked you that?

speaker: Witness B
text: The deputy, when I gave my statement. And my sister. And the lawyers when I met with them. I tell everybody the same thing.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Move to strike the nonresponsive portion.

speaker: Attorney
text: Your objection is noted. When you gave your written statement to the deputy a few days later, did you describe the car's approach?

speaker: Witness B
text: I did. Not as much as today. It was short. But I wrote that I saw the car come over the hill and I saw it hit.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is anything you've told me today about the car different from what you wrote in that statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Today's just more detail because you're asking more questions.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Let me ask about the moments just before the hit. Did you see the car swerve?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't see it swerve.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see it move left or right in its lane?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I could tell. It just kept going straight.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see any smoke or dust from the tires before the contact?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the car's speed seem any different right before the contact than it did coming down the hill?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Objection. Foundation. Form.

speaker: Witness B
text: It looked the same to me. Fast. Same as it had been.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you don't have a number for that speed.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I told you, fast. Highway speed. That's all I can say.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. Have you ever driven that stretch yourself coming down that hill eastbound?

speaker: Witness B
text: Lots of times. Every week, like I said before.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you drive it, what speed do you usually go?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to relevance. But go ahead.

speaker: Witness B
text: The speed limit, more or less. I don't speed. My car's old.

speaker: Attorney
text: Without guessing at a number, would you say the car you saw was going faster or slower than you usually drive that hill?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Objection. Foundation. Calls for speculation.

speaker: Witness B
text: Faster, I'd say. But I really can't give you a number. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just don't know.

speaker: Attorney
text: You're not being difficult. That's exactly the kind of answer I need. If you don't know, tell me you don't know.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask a few questions about time. Do you know what time it was when you first noticed the car coming over the hill?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not exactly. It was around four-thirty, a little after. I'd been out there a while waiting.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you checked the time recently?

speaker: Witness B
text: A little before. My sister said she'd be there around five, and I remember thinking I still had a while.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where did you check the time?

speaker: Witness B
text: My watch. I wear a watch. I don't like taking my phone out.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before the dark car came over the hill, how many other eastbound cars had you watched come over that hill while you were waiting?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't know. Some. Not a lot. It wasn't busy. Maybe a car every little while.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any of those other cars stand out to you?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just regular traffic.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the road surface wet or dry?

speaker: Witness B
text: Dry. It hadn't rained. It was a clear day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any wind?

speaker: Witness B
text: A little breeze. Nothing much.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any haze, glare off the road, anything that made it harder to see down the road to the west?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was a clear day. You could see a long way.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. I want to ask you one more time about the approach, and then we'll move on. From the time the car came over the crest to the moment of contact, was there anything at all that came between you and the car?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Asked and answered.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear anything at the moment of contact?

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll get to the sound and what happened after in more detail later this morning. For now, is there anything else about the car's approach that you remember that we haven't covered?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. It came over the hill, it came down fast, it didn't slow down, and it hit. That's what I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you have any trouble seeing the color of the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was dark. I said black or dark gray, something like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice anything on the car, any marks, any roof rack, anything unusual?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a plain dark car. Nothing on top of it that I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you ever seen that car before that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not that I know of.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see where the car came from before it came over the hill?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. You can't see past the hill from there. The first I saw it was when it came over the top.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Let me take a step back. You've said a couple of times that you watched the car the whole way in. Was that something you thought about at the time, or something you realized afterward?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't understand the question.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Let me try again. At the time you were watching the car, did you think to yourself, I'm watching this car?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. You don't think like that. I was just looking at it. Afterward I knew I'd seen the whole thing.

speaker: Attorney
text: When did you first tell someone that you had seen the car come in?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Objection. Hearsay. Move to strike.

speaker: Attorney
text: Noted. I'm not asking what the store employee said. I'm just asking about timing. That was within a few minutes of the crash?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few minutes. Maybe less. She came right out.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll come back to that conversation later. Have you ever had any problem with your distance vision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. My eyes are fine far away. I had them checked last year for my license.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you pass?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. No restrictions except reading.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything about how you were feeling that afternoon, tired, sick, anything, that would have affected what you saw?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I felt fine. I'd just done my shopping. I was just waiting.

speaker: Attorney
text: I think that covers the car's approach. In a moment I'm going to turn to the truck. Before I do, is there anything you've said about the car that you'd like to change or correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. That's all true.

speaker: Attorney
text: Counsel, I'm about to move on to a new subject. Do you need anything before I do?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: No, go ahead.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Just one more on the car. When the car came down the hill, you said you watched it from the top. How would you describe the grade, the slope of the hill, from what you could see?

speaker: Witness B
text: Gentle. It's not steep. It just goes down a little toward the intersection, and then it's flat there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the slope affect your ability to see the car at all?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. If anything, it made it easier, because it was coming down toward me. I could see it fine.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Let's turn to the truck.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. I want to shift now from the car to the truck. Is that okay with you?

speaker: Witness B
text: That's fine.

speaker: Attorney
text: At some point that afternoon, before the crash, did you notice a large truck near the intersection?

speaker: Witness B

text: Was it in one of the westbound travel lanes, or somewhere else?

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney
text: Just so the record is clear, that's the turn lane on the westbound side that lets you turn left across the median toward 140th?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That one.

speaker: Attorney
text: How did you know it was in the turn lane and not the regular lane?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because it was over on the left, by the median, where the lane cuts in. The regular lanes were to the right of it, and cars were going by it in those.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see cars going by it in the westbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: A couple, I think. Not a lot. It wasn't busy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Tell me what you remember about the truck itself. Start with the trailer.

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Witness B

text: Could you hear that hum from where you were outside the store?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney
text: What about the cab, the tractor part. What do you remember about that?

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you have any estimate of how long the trailer was?

speaker: Witness B
text: Long. The regular long kind. I couldn't give you feet. I'm not good with distances, I said that before.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Would you say it was the size of trailer you typically see on the highway, the big ones?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Leading.

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney
text: When you first noticed the truck in the turn lane, was it stopped, or was it moving?

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll rephrase. From where you were, which way did the cab appear to be heading as it crossed?

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I could tell. It was kind of steady. Slow and steady. Maybe it picked up a little once it was moving. I really don't know.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see it stop at any point during the turn, before the crash?

speaker: Opposing counsel

text: I'm not asking you to make anything up. If you don't know, that's a fine answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Then I don't know the exact number. It was a few seconds, and it was slow.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the engine noise change during the turn?

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Opposing counsel

speaker: Attorney
text: If you know.

speaker: Opposing counsel

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Asked and answered.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's my memory. Car over the hill, truck starts across, about together or right after.

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Witness B
text: The right lane. The outside one, nearest the store. Like I said before.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the car stay in that lane while the truck was turning?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It stayed right there. Straight.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the car move toward the left lane, or toward the shoulder, at any point while the truck was crossing?

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney

speaker: Witness B
text: No. No horn from anybody.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just before the impact, where was the truck?

speaker: Witness B

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the truck still moving at that moment?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think so. Still slow. Still going.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the car, just before the impact, where was it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Right there. In the right lane, coming up to the trailer.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which part of the truck did the car come up on? The cab, the trailer?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: The trailer. The side of the trailer. Not the cab. The cab was already past.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know about where along the trailer? Front, middle, back?

speaker: Witness B
text: Somewhere in the middle, more toward the back maybe. Behind the cab, ahead of the back wheels. I couldn't tell you exactly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. We'll come back to that. I want to ask a few more general things about the truck. Had you seen that truck before that day, at the store or on the road?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not that I know of. Lots of trucks go through there. I wouldn't know one from another.

speaker: Attorney
text: Going back to that afternoon. While the truck was in the turn lane, before it started across, did you see anything about the truck that seemed unusual to you?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a truck waiting to turn. Nothing stood out. I didn't think anything of it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see any doors open on it, anything loose, anything like that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Did the trailer at any point cross into the area of 140th itself, before the crash?

speaker: Witness B
text: The front part of the truck was going into 140th. The trailer was still mostly on the highway when it happened.

speaker: Attorney
text: How much of the truck, if any, was on 140th at the moment of the crash, if you can say?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: The cab, maybe. Starting onto it. Maybe a little of the front of the trailer. I can't say exactly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Let me ask it this way. Was the cab on the highway or past the highway when the crash happened?

speaker: Witness B
text: At the edge, or just past it. Going onto 140th. It was most of the way through the turn with the front end.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you're describing the cab's position there based on what you saw at the time?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Based on what I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. One moment.

speaker: Attorney
text: I want to make sure I have the timeline straight. You noticed the truck sitting in the westbound turn lane, stopped or creeping, correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: You don't know how long it had been there?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: At about the time the car came over the hill, the truck began its turn?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Mischaracterizes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is that a fair summary of what you said?

speaker: Witness B
text: About that time, or right after. Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: The truck moved out of the turn lane, through the crossover, and across the eastbound lanes, toward 140th?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Slowly?

speaker: Witness B
text: Slowly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Without stopping, that you saw?

speaker: Witness B
text: Without stopping that I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: And at some point the trailer was across both eastbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Both of them.

text: And during that time, you didn't hear a horn and you didn't hear brakes?

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything about the truck's movements that you remember that I haven't asked you about?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. That's what I remember. It came across slow, and the trailer was across the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you say anything out loud, or call out, while the truck was turning?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. There wasn't time to say anything, and I don't know who I would have said it to. I was just standing there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was anyone else outside the store with you during the truck's turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not right with me. I don't remember anybody else outside right then. The girl who worked there was inside.

speaker: Attorney
text: How do you know she was inside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because she came out after. After the crash. She came out the door.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll get to that. Before the crash, did you see anyone else on the store property, in the lot?

speaker: Witness B
text: There might have been a car parked. I don't remember people. It was quiet.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just a few more about the truck. After the truck got across, and we'll talk about this more later, did you see where it ended up?

speaker: Witness B
text: It went on down 140th. It kept going a ways and stopped down there past the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll come back to exactly where. Did it stop right away, or keep going?

speaker: Witness B
text: It kept going a little. It didn't stop right at the highway. It went down some and then stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. We'll pick that up later this morning. I'm going to move now to the moment of impact, which is the next area.

speaker: Attorney
text: I want to move now to the collision itself. I'm going to ask you about what you heard and what you saw, and then about what happened afterward. All right?

speaker: Witness B
text: All right.

speaker: Attorney
text: What is the first thing you noticed at the moment of the impact?

speaker: Witness B
text: The sound. It was the loudest thing I ever heard. It was like a bang and a scrape at the same time, metal on metal.

text: How long did the sound last, as best you can estimate?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe a second or two for the main part. Then there was more noise after, further off. I'll get to that, I guess.

text: No horn. I didn't hear a horn.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are you saying there was no such sound, or that you don't recall one?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

text: I'm saying I didn't hear one. If there was one, I didn't hear it.

speaker: Attorney
text: If you know.

text: The south side, that's the same side of the highway as the store?

text: About how fast was the car moving after it came out from under the trailer?

speaker: Opposing counsel

text: At least two. I think two. There may have been more. It was getting further away by then.

text: What kind of fences were they, if you remember?

text: Was the car moving in a straight line or was it turning?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.
