text: When you say the pole moved, what did you see?

speaker: Witness B
text: It shook. It leaned. I remember the wires swinging. I thought the lines were going to come down.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did they come down?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. Not that I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how far away from the intersection was that pole?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Calls for speculation.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just your best estimate.

speaker: Witness B
text: Far. A long way. I'd say a couple football fields, maybe more. I told the deputy it was way down there. I'm not good with distances, I said that before.

speaker: Attorney
text: I understand. Did the car come to a stop after it hit the pole?

speaker: Witness B
text: It went a little further after that, I think, and then it stopped. It ended up in somebody's yard down there. There's a house back off the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you see the car once it stopped?

speaker: Witness B
text: I could see it was there. I could see the shape of it. It was a long way off. I couldn't see details.

speaker: Attorney
text: From the time of the first bang to the time you saw the car hit the pole, how long was that?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: A few seconds. It felt longer. It felt like it went on and on, but it was probably only a few seconds.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me turn to the truck. What did the truck do after the impact?

speaker: Witness B
text: It kept going a little. It finished the turn, kind of. It went on across and down 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: Down 140th, meaning south?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, south. Down the side road, past the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the truck stop?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It stopped down there on 140th. South of the store some ways.

speaker: Attorney
text: How far south of the store, if you can estimate?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that far. The whole truck was past the corner, I think. The back of the trailer was down past the edge of the store lot. Something like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did it stop quickly or slowly, as far as you could tell?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't know. It wasn't sudden, like a slam. It just rolled down there and stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see any damage to the trailer from where you were?

speaker: Witness B
text: I saw it later, when it was stopped. The side was messed up. There was a big dent, kind of torn along the bottom edge. I didn't go up close to it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which side of the trailer was damaged?

speaker: Witness B
text: The side that had been facing the car. After it turned, that side was facing kind of west, toward the road. I could see it.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not going to ask you about any person. I just want to understand where you were and what you did. Immediately after the car hit the pole, what did you do?

speaker: Witness B
text: I just stood there. I couldn't move for a second. I think I said something out loud, like oh my God. I dropped my bag.

speaker: Attorney
text: The shopping bag you mentioned earlier?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Stuff went all over. I didn't even care. I left it there for a while.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you move from where you were standing?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not much. I stayed out front of the store. I took a couple steps, toward the road, and then I stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why did you stop?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because I didn't know what to do. There were cars still coming on the highway, I didn't want to walk out there. And it was so far down there where the car was.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you ever walk down to where the car came to rest?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't go down there. I didn't want to see. I'll be honest about that.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Nobody is going to ask you to describe anything you didn't see. Did anyone else go down there that you saw?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some people stopped their cars on the highway and ran down there. A couple of people. I don't know who they were.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how many vehicles stopped, if you remember?

speaker: Witness B
text: Two or three at first. Then more. After a while there were cars pulled off everywhere.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you make a phone call at some point?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I called my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: How soon after the crash did you call her?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few minutes. Maybe a minute or two. I had to find my phone, it was in my bag and the bag was on the ground.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you call 911?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I thought about it, but somebody said they already called. And then the lady from the store came out and said she called.

speaker: Attorney
text: Who said they already called, the first time?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not asking for the truth of it. Just who said it, if you know.

speaker: Witness B
text: One of the people who stopped. A man, I think. He yelled it. I don't know him.

speaker: Attorney
text: What did you say to your sister on the phone?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: I told her there was a terrible wreck right in front of the store and to hurry up, and that she should be careful coming because the road was going to be blocked.

speaker: Attorney
text: What did she say?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Same objection.

speaker: Witness B
text: She said she was close and she was coming. That's about it. I was crying, so it was hard to talk.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's talk about the store employee. At some point did someone come out of the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The woman who worked the counter. She came running out.

speaker: Attorney
text: How soon after the crash did she come out?

speaker: Witness B
text: Pretty fast. Right after. Maybe while I was still standing there. Before I called my sister, I think. Or around the same time. I'm not sure of the order.

speaker: Attorney
text: When she came out, did you talk with her?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Tell me what you said to her.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: These are her own statements. You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: I told her a car went under the truck. I told her it went way down there and hit the pole. I was pointing. I was pretty upset. I don't remember every word.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did she ask you any questions?

speaker: Witness B
text: She asked me what happened. She asked if I was okay. She asked if anybody called for help.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did she stay with you?

speaker: Witness B
text: For a little while. Then she went back in and out a couple of times. She was on the phone, I think.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you tell her anything else about what you saw?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: Probably. I was talking a lot. I kept saying it over and over. I think I said I saw the whole thing. I know I said that to a lot of people that day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember anything she said to you, other than the questions?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Hearsay.

speaker: Witness B
text: She said something like she didn't see it, she just heard it from inside. She said it shook the windows. Something like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the two of you talk about where you were standing?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't remember that. I don't think we talked about it like that. We were just talking about the wreck.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Did any police or emergency vehicles arrive?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Deputies came. And an ambulance, and the fire truck, I think. A bunch of them.

speaker: Attorney
text: How long after the crash did the first one arrive?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: It felt like forever. But it was probably ten minutes. Maybe less. I really don't know.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any of them stop at the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Later, yes. A deputy car parked up by the crossover with the lights on. And they started blocking the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did they close the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: The eastbound side, at least. They were waving people around. It was a while before cars could get through.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was your sister able to get to the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. She got there around five. She had to come around a different way, I think, or they let her through. She pulled into the store lot.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you leave when your sister arrived?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not right away. I wanted to tell somebody what I saw. I thought somebody should know.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you speak to a deputy that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. One of them came up to the store. He was asking if anybody saw it.

speaker: Attorney
text: What did you tell him?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: I told him I saw it. I told him I saw the car come down the hill and go under the truck. I told him it went down there and hit the pole.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the deputy write anything down?

speaker: Witness B
text: He wrote some things in a little notebook. He took my name and my phone number and my address.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did he ask you to give a written statement that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, not that day. He said somebody would contact me. And then a few days later they did, and I wrote it out. That's the statement I looked at before today.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll talk about that statement in more detail later. How long did you talk with the deputy that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not long. Five minutes. He was busy. There were a lot of people.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did he ask you where you were when it happened?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: He asked if I was there. I said I was out front of the store. I don't think he asked more than that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did he show you anything, a diagram, a photo, anything like that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any other official talk with you that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember. Just the one deputy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the truck get moved while you were there?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was still sitting down on 140th when we left.

speaker: Attorney
text: About what time did you leave?

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe five thirty. Quarter to six. It was still light out.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone tell you anything about the people in the car?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object. Calls for hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll withdraw that. Let me ask it differently. Did you yourself see anything about the condition of anyone in the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't go down there, and I didn't see anything like that. I'd rather not talk about that part.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. I'm not going to ask you about that. Let me go back to a couple of things. You said the car went off the south side of the road. Do you know about where along the highway it left the pavement?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: Not exactly. A ways past the intersection. Past the store. Further down.

speaker: Attorney
text: Past the store to the east?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, east.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see where the car went relative to the store itself? Did it come near the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, it didn't come near the store. It was out on the road and then off past it, down the shoulder and into the field.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there any other vehicle on the eastbound side of the highway at the moment of the impact, that you saw?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not right there. There was nobody else right there that I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about on the westbound side?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't remember anything on the westbound side right then. Maybe something further off. Nothing close.

speaker: Attorney
text: After the impact, did any eastbound cars come over the hill?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. A minute or so after, I think, a car came over and slowed way down. Then pulled over. That might have been one of the ones that stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any vehicle have to go around the truck on the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, by then the truck was already off the highway. It was down 140th. The road was clear except for, you know, pieces.

speaker: Attorney
text: Pieces of what?

speaker: Witness B
text: Debris. Glass and parts. There was stuff on the road by the crossover. I could see it shining.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you touch or pick up any of that debris?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't go out on the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: At any point that afternoon, did you go out into the highway or the median?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed by the store the whole time.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say by the store, you mean out front, the area you've described?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Out front. And inside that one time.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Did your sister see the crash?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. She wasn't there yet. She came after.

speaker: Attorney
text: When your sister arrived, did you tell her what you saw?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, I told her the whole thing in the car on the way home. I told her again later too. I couldn't stop talking about it.

speaker: Attorney
text: How were you feeling physically that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: Shaky. My legs were like jelly. I wasn't hurt. I was just upset. I didn't sleep good that night.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thinking back on everything that happened after the impact, from the bang to the time you left, is there anything you saw that you haven't told us about today?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. I think I've told you all of it. The bang, the car going down there, the pole, the truck stopping. The lady from the store. The deputies.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything about what you heard that you haven't told us?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just that it was loud. Then after, it got real quiet for a little bit. Except the truck. That hum kept going. I remember that.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. I'm going to shift gears in a moment to your written statement and some other things. Before I do, is there anything about your answers in the last few minutes that you want to change or add to?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. That's what I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Thank you. Let's keep going.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's keep going. I want to circle back to a few things from earlier before I show you a document. Are you doing all right? Do you need water or anything?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'm fine. I have water. Thank you.

speaker: Attorney
text: Earlier you told us your sister picked you up that afternoon. About what time did she get there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Around five. Maybe a couple of minutes after.

speaker: Attorney
text: So from the time of the collision until your sister arrived, about how long was that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Twenty-five minutes, something like that. It felt longer.

speaker: Attorney
text: During those twenty-five minutes, did you stay at the store the entire time?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I didn't leave the store property. I stayed out front.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you ever walk down the highway toward where the car ended up?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't go down there. I didn't want to.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you walk down Northeast 140th Court toward the truck?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed up by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: When your sister arrived, where did she park?

speaker: Witness B
text: In the little lot by the store. She couldn't get in easy because of all the deputies' cars, but she squeezed in.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you tell her what had happened?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some. Not a lot right then. I was pretty shook up. I told her more on the drive home.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form, to the extent it calls for the content of conversations.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not asking what you said yet. Just whether you talked about it. You did?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, on the way home.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did your sister see any part of the collision herself?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. She wasn't there yet. She came after.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before we get to the exhibit, a few more questions about that afternoon. When the deputies arrived, about how many were there?

speaker: Witness B
text: At first one car, then more. Four or five cars, I think, and then the fire trucks and the ambulance came.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any of them come from the west, the same direction the car had come from?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some of them did. Some came from the other way. I really couldn't tell you which ones.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were the eastbound lanes blocked off at some point?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. They put cars across the road and were waving traffic around. It got backed up up toward the hill.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see anyone take photographs or measurements while you were there?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: I saw a deputy with a camera, I think. And later somebody with a tape, a long tape, on the road. I didn't watch closely.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone ask you to point anything out on the road while you were there?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. The deputy just asked what I saw and wrote it on a pad. Then he said someone might call me.

speaker: Attorney
text: And did someone call you?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, a few days later. That's when I did the written one.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where did you write it?

speaker: Witness B
text: At the sheriff's office. They had me sit at a table and write it out by hand, and then I signed it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone tell you what to put in it?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. They just said write down what you saw, in your own words.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. You mentioned a deputy took your information that afternoon. Did that deputy ask you to write anything down that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, not that day. He took my name and number and asked me a few questions. The written one was later.

speaker: Attorney
text: And that written statement is the one we've talked about this morning, the one you reviewed before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's the one.

speaker: Attorney
text: Between the day of the collision and the day you wrote that statement, did you go back to the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: I drove past it. I didn't stop.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why didn't you stop?

speaker: Witness B
text: I just didn't want to. It was still too fresh.

speaker: Attorney
text: Since then, have you stopped at that store again?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few times. It's the closest store to my sister's place. I go in and out. I don't really hang around out front anymore.

speaker: Attorney
text: Has anything about the intersection changed since that day, as far as you can tell?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just from your own observation, driving through.

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I noticed. The road looks the same to me. Same store, same side road. I don't pay much attention to it now, honestly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Now, before I show you the exhibit, I want to make sure I understand some directions, so we're using the same words. The highway runs east and west there, correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. East and west.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the car you've described was traveling east?

speaker: Witness B
text: East. Coming from the hill side, from the west.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the truck was in the westbound lanes, in the turn lane, before it turned?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. In the turn lane on the other side of the median.

speaker: Attorney
text: And Northeast 140th Court runs which direction off the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: South. It goes south, down past the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the store is on which side of 140th Court?

speaker: Witness B
text: The east side. The store's on the corner there, on the south side of the highway.

speaker: Attorney
text: When the truck turned, which direction did it turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: Left. From where it was, it turned left, across our side of the highway and onto 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say 'our side,' you mean the eastbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, sorry. The eastbound lanes. The side by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: No need to apologize. That's exactly why I'm asking. I'd like to show you what we'll mark as Exhibit 4.

speaker: Attorney
text: For the record, Exhibit 4 is an aerial-style map of the intersection of U.S. 27A and Northeast 140th Court. I'm handing a copy to the witness and a copy to counsel.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Thank you. I'll note for the record that this is a demonstrative and we haven't stipulated to its scale or accuracy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. Ma'am, take a moment to look it over. Have you ever seen this document before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I've never seen this.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you seen any map or photograph of the intersection taken from above, before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember. Maybe on a phone map, years ago, but not for this.

speaker: Attorney
text: Take your time with it. Do you recognize what's shown?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's the highway, going across. That's the median in the middle with the grass. And this is the crossover where the truck turned.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you see the side road, Northeast 140th Court?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, here, going down. Going south.

speaker: Attorney
text: And do you see the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's the building, here. That's the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you see the lanes of the highway, the two eastbound lanes and the two westbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Two and two, with the grass between them.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you see the crossover, the paved opening in the median?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, right here, lined up with the side road.

speaker: Attorney
text: And to the right of the store, to the east, is there anything you recognize?

speaker: Witness B
text: That's the field and the fences, going down toward where the houses are. The car went off down that way, but it's further than this shows.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the place where the car came to rest isn't on this map?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. It was way down. Past the edge here.

speaker: Attorney
text: There's an arrow in the corner of the map marked with an N. Do you understand that to point north?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the top of the page is north, the bottom is south, the left side is west, and the right side is east. Is that how you understand it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, that makes sense. The hill would be off this way, to the left, off the page.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Is there anything on this map that looks wrong to you, compared to how you remember the intersection?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Not really. It's a picture from the top, so it looks different than standing there. But the road and the store look right to me.

speaker: Attorney
text: Does the map, in general, fairly show the layout of the roads and the store as they were on May 7th, 2016, as best you can tell?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Same objection. Foundation.

speaker: Witness B
text: As best I can tell, yes. The roads are where they were.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm going to ask you to make some marks on this map. I'm handing you a pen. It's a red pen, so the marks will show up. Please don't make any marks until I ask you to. Okay?

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: And if you're not sure about something, it's fine to tell me that instead of marking. I don't want you to guess.

speaker: Witness B
text: All right.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's start with the truck. Before it began its turn, you said it was in the westbound left-turn lane. Do you see that turn lane on the map?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It's this little lane right by the median, on the top side.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not going to have you mark that. I just want to make sure we're oriented. Now, after the collision, did the truck keep moving?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It kept going. It went on down the side road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you watch it come to a stop?

speaker: Witness B
text: I saw it stopped. I saw it sitting there down the road. I don't know if I saw the exact second it stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. How long after the collision did you notice it stopped?

speaker: Witness B
text: Pretty quick. Seconds. I looked that way and it was stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you first noticed the truck stopped, were you looking south down 140th?

speaker: Witness B
text: I turned and looked that way, yes. Everybody was looking every which way. It was loud and then it was quiet.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the truck's engine still running, as far as you could hear?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think so. I remember a rumbling for a while. I couldn't tell you when it stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before the collision, as the truck began turning, was it moving in a straight line or a curve?

speaker: Witness B
text: A curve, the way you'd turn. The cab went first and the trailer swung around behind it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Using the pen, please mark where the truck came to a stop.

speaker: Witness B
text: It was down here. Down 140th, past the store. About here.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Would you put the number 1 next to that mark?

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay. There. Number 1.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is that mark where the front of the truck was, the back of the trailer, or somewhere in between?

speaker: Witness B
text: I was just marking the truck. Where the truck part was, the cab. The trailer was behind it, back toward the highway.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the trailer still extend back toward the highway after it stopped?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some of it, yes. It's a long trailer. I couldn't tell you exactly how much.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Did the truck move again after that, while you were there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I saw. It stayed there. The deputies were all around it after a while.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember anyone getting into or out of the truck?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't remember that. I wasn't looking at it the whole time. I was mostly looking the other way, down the highway, and then at my phone calling my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. I want to go back to the moment the car reached the intersection. You've told us this morning you were outside, out front of the store. Correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long had you been there, outside, by the time the car reached the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: A good while. I'd done my shopping and come out, and I'd been waiting maybe fifteen, twenty minutes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you standing or sitting at that point?

speaker: Witness B
text: Standing. I'd been standing a while. I had my bag at my feet.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'd like you to show us on the map.

speaker: Attorney
text: And please mark where you were standing when the car reached the intersection.

speaker: Witness B
text: I was over by the corner, near the shelter.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Let the record reflect the witness has marked Exhibit 4. Would you put the number 2 next to that mark?

speaker: Witness B
text: Number 2. Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: And would you put your initials and today's date at the bottom of the page?

speaker: Witness B
text: Here?

speaker: Attorney
text: Anywhere at the bottom is fine.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay. Done.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you in that same general spot the whole time the car was approaching, from when you first saw it?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Compound.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll rephrase. From when you first noticed the car until the collision, did you move from where you were?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I was just standing there waiting. I wasn't walking around.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. At this time I'll offer Exhibit 4, as marked by the witness, into the record.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: No objection to it being attached to the transcript, subject to the objection I made earlier as to scale and accuracy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. I'll pass the witness. Counsel, do you have questions?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Just a few. Ma'am, I represent the motor carrier. I'll be brief. You understand you're still under oath?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Before today, had anyone shown you Exhibit 4?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Today's the first time.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: When you made the marks on Exhibit 4 a few minutes ago, did anyone help you decide where to put them?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody helped me. I did it myself.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Did anyone point to a spot on the map or suggest a spot to you, either today or before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Did you discuss with anyone, before today, where you would mark on a map?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't know there was going to be a map.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: The mark you labeled number 2. How sure are you of that spot?

speaker: Witness B
text: Roughly, yes. I'm sure of it roughly. I wasn't measuring where my feet were. But that's about where I was.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Could you have been a few feet one way or another from that mark?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few feet, maybe. It's a little mark on a big picture. But that's the area.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: And the mark you labeled number 1, for where the truck stopped. Same question. How sure are you of that one?

speaker: Witness B
text: About the same. That's about where it was. I wouldn't swear to the exact foot.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: You'd never seen a picture of the intersection from above before today, correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Correct.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: So you were translating what you saw standing on the ground onto a picture from overhead.

speaker: Attorney
text: Object to form.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: I guess so. But I know that corner. I've been to that store a hundred times.

text: Before today, did you ever go back and stand in the spot you marked, to check what you could see from there?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I never did anything like that.

text: Has anyone, an investigator or anyone else, asked you to go out to the intersection with them?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody's asked me to do that.

text: Did you bring any notes or drawings with you today?

text: No. Just my glasses and my water.

text: You mentioned earlier you wear reading glasses. Were you wearing them when you marked the exhibit?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, to see the little lines on the map. I don't wear them for distance. I didn't have them on that day outside.

text: Understood. Last thing. Other than your written statement and what you've told us here today, have you given any other statement about what you saw, written or recorded?
